_comment: The Apps Script source manifest — the single list of files that make up the
deployed script. Every consumer reads this instead of hardcoding a filename:
the four test suites, scripts/patch_version.js, scripts/validate.py,
scripts/prod_health.py, the .claspignore hygiene check, and the deploy
workflow's syntax lint, push order and deployed-file assertion.
It exists so that splitting SpamDetector.gs into several .gs files is a pure
file move: nothing outside this manifest needs to learn the new names.
Read it via scripts/sources.js (Node) or scripts/sources.py (Python) rather
than parsing it again by hand — a third parser is a third thing to drift.
sources    — concatenation AND clasp push order. Apps Script has no module
system: all files share one global scope. SpamDetector.gs has no
top-level executed statements and no cross-references between
top-level initializers, so order does not affect behaviour today;
it is pinned anyway, and emitted as filePushOrder at deploy time,
so the concatenation CI lints is the one Apps Script builds.
versionFile — the one file carrying both version markers ('* @version X.Y.Z'
and 'const SCRIPT_VERSION'). patch_version.js rewrites only this
file; validate.py asserts the markers appear exactly once across
the whole manifest, so a stray copy elsewhere is caught.
